ecstatic

ek-STAT-ik -- stress on the second syllable, STAT. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Ecstatic is full of overwhelming joy.

The whole village was ecstatic when the home team carried the national trophy down Main Street for the first time.

Worked Example

The shelter door opens, his lost dog bounds straight into his arms, and the boy laughs and cries at the same time, spinning them both in circles.

Joy that overwhelming -- too big for a smile, spilling out as laughter, tears, and spinning -- is what ecstatic means. It sits far above 'happy' or 'pleased' on the joy scale.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

overjoyed: Overjoyed means extremely happy about something -- the plainest of the strong-joy words. Ecstatic goes past it: the joy is overwhelming, too big to hold in, spilling into laughter or tears. You can be overjoyed and still finish your sentence; ecstatic people usually cannot.

euphoric: Euphoric names a floating, whole-body wave of happiness -- the world feels weightless, and the feeling can arrive without any single cause. Ecstatic is overwhelming joy at something: a win, a reunion, big news. Euphoria is a state you drift in; ecstatic is a reaction.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

miserable: deeply unhappy

despondent: in very low spirits, without hope

Where it sits · how intense the happiness is — thrilled → ecstatic → delirious

thrilled vs. ecstatic: Thrilled is strong but still a rung below ecstatic -- a thrilled winner beams and cheers, while an ecstatic one is beside themselves, joy overflowing beyond any control.

delirious vs. ecstatic: Delirious pushes past even ecstatic: an ecstatic winner is overwhelmed with joy, while a delirious one is so far gone that thought scrambles and the celebration turns into a dizzy blur.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ec-

Prefix — ec-: out (Greek ek-)

Root — stat

Root — stat: to stand (from Greek histanai/stasis -- the same root in stationary and static)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: having the characteristics of; like (Greek -ikos, via Latin -icus)

Put it together

Put it together: Ec- ('out', Greek ek-) + stat ('to stand', from Greek histanai) + -ic spell ecstatic. Greek ekstasis meant 'a standing outside oneself': joy this big pushes you right out of your ordinary self -- when you are ecstatic, you are quite literally 'beside yourself' with happiness.

Use the root in a new word: stationary

Use the root in a new word: stationary: The traffic sat completely stationary for an hour after the parade closed Main Street.

Root Check

Word Choice

Save ecstatic for the top of the joy scale -- news that makes people scream, dance, or cry happy tears. It often appears as 'absolutely ecstatic' and takes 'about' or 'at': ecstatic about the results, ecstatic at the news.
